memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Woe to you, Moab! You are destroyed, people of Chemosh! He has given up his sons as fugitives and his daughters as captives to Sihon king of the Amorites. But we have overthrown them; Heshbon's dominion has been destroyed all the way to Dibon. We have demolished them as far as Nophah, which extends to Medeba. - Num 21:29-30 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The old poem continues, and now it names Moab's god, Chemosh. The verse mocks the helplessness of this idol. Chemosh could not protect his own people; he gave up his sons and daughters to the enemy. The god the Moabites trusted was powerless to save them.

This is the truth about every false god. Whatever we look to for security and salvation apart from the living God will fail us in the end. Idols make grand promises but cannot deliver. When the crisis comes, they have no power to help, no strength to save.

We may not bow to statues of Chemosh, but our hearts are still prone to trust in idols of another kind. Money, status, relationships, our own abilities: any of these can quietly take the place that belongs to God alone. And like Chemosh, they will let us down when we need them most.

How different is the living God. He does not abandon His children in their hour of need. In Christ we have a Saviour who did not give up His people but gave up Himself for them (Gal 2:20). Turn from every empty idol and trust the God who truly saves.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What "idols" are you tempted to trust instead of the living God?
2. Where has something you relied on let you down?
3. How does Christ's faithfulness contrast with the emptiness of false gods?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Living God, expose the idols in my heart and turn me from them. Help me to trust in Christ alone, who did not abandon me but gave Himself for me. Amen.
